Now let's confirm where these dispatch functions are called (memo create/update/delete/comment create) to verify the "lifecycle events".

q30.

- memo created: `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:15`, called from `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:157`)
- memo updated: `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:20`, called from `server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go:67`)
- memo deleted: `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:25`, called from `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:562`)
- memo comment created: `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:30`, called from `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:119`)

All four converge in `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` (the created/updated/deleted ones call this shared helper directly at `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:48`; the comment-created one duplicates the same body inline) which, along with the comment handler, ultimately calls `webhook.PostAsync` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:184`). `PostAsync` enqueues the payload onto `asyncPostQueue`, which is drained by worker goroutines that call `webhook.Post` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`) — this `Post` function is where the actual HTTP delivery (signing + `safeClient.Do(req)`) happens, so it is the true final convergence point for delivery.
